correctness.rationale: Every rational canonical primary summand is accounted for. The Hom dimension d_f min(s,t) gives D; endomorphism ring modulo Jacobson radical is a product of M_m(F_{q^d}), with radical of dimension r, and each unit tuple has q^r lifts. On each f^s filtration a diagonal endomorphism has s identical residual F_{q^d}-linear traces; off-diagonal maps contribute none. The matrix Gauss sum equals (-1)^m Q^{m(m-1)/2}, proved directly via subspace-lattice Möbius inversion. Fourier inversion yields T_A(0) and T_A(b) for all b, with every p|s boundary handled. The bundled checker independently exhausts all commuting units for 45 selected q=2,3,4,5 examples, including f of degrees 2 and 3 and unequal block lengths, and ends VERIFY_OK; such tests do not replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: The complete arbitrary-similarity-type invertible-centralizer trace distribution, including the characteristic-divisible block-length bias B, is not stated in the materially read full texts or the retrieved published research findings. Li–Hu 2011 Theorem 3.1 already covers scalar A and is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim; Britnell–Wildon 2010 computes determinants and centralizer-module composition multiplicities but does not enumerate trace fibers. The classical centralizer group order and Gauss identity are credited as inputs. The structurally relevant 2019 arXiv:1909.06198 source was inspected in full open-access text, including its §§4–6, and no such trace-fiber result was found.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent two-level trace enumeration may exist in unindexed or differently termed literature; database search alone is not uniqueness proof.

Britnell–Wildon structural decomposition and Li–Hu matrix-group Fourier evaluation are strong known ingredients; novelty is the explicit exact synthesis for arbitrary centralizer units, not either ingredient.

value.rationale: The problem is a natural centralizer-refined version of the classical full-GL prescribed-trace census and complements determinant-image studies for all finite-field similarity types. It supplies one exact product formula for every rational canonical type, detects a characteristic-dependent trace-blindness boundary (all block lengths divisible by p), and recovers all other trace fibers including cases where they vanish. This is a complete invariant and nontrivial Fourier/endomorphism-algebra synthesis, not an isolated small parameter calculation.
